svg.title: Cisco voice sessions and incoming-call priority
svg.desc: Both lines share one physical phone and one bounded manual voice owner. The gateway serializes voice Start with direct phone mutations. Active or uncertain ownership blocks direct dial, speaker, remote answer and display commands. Incoming SIP calls, including eligible ring and timer or alarm calls, remain allowed. Either line becoming busy or ringing causes the AMI observer to stop the owned RTP session. Optional automatic answer waits for cleanup; a pre-I/O refusal does not consume its attempt, but an ambiguous I/O result does. Timer and alarm alerts never auto-answer.

g.text: Voice sessions yield to incoming calls
Current gateway: explicit manual Start · at most 30 seconds · no automatic restart into listening
ONE PHYSICAL PHONE
Cisco 7945G
Line A
Line B
One audio path, one voice owner
SERIALIZED ADMISSION
Start + direct phone changes
Shared gateway mutation lock
Fresh media / call checks before I/O
Either alias resolves to the same handset.
BOUNDED VOICE OWNERSHIP
Active or cleanup uncertain
Ownership survives separate requests.
Process exit alone is not Stop proof.
No unrelated RTP Stop to force a command.
TWO DIFFERENT PATHS WHILE VOICE OWNS THE PHONE
Direct phone changes: refused
Dial · speaker key · remote answer · display
voice_phone_busy — do not overwrite the audio owner
Intercom checks both phones. Both line aliases are covered.
Uncertain cleanup continues to block conflicting actions.
Incoming SIP: retains priority
Ordinary calls · gateway ring · timer / alarm alert
Existing busy, DND and active-alert checks still apply.
Voice ownership alone does not suppress these calls.
The arriving call triggers the media controller below.
1. Observe both lines
AMI reports ringing or busy.
Stale or failed observation also
ends the voice session.
2. Stop owned RTP
Stop capture and playback.
Keep cleanup evidence.
No automatic voice rearm.
3. Optional automatic answer
Wait for cleanup; recheck the exact call.
Pre-I/O refusal: attempt is still available.
Ambiguous I/O: no repeat key press for that call.
Timer and alarm alerts never auto-answer.
Still available: exact-call hangup · alert Stop · exact-session voice Stop · preferences
The 30-second software lease is not a demonstrated hardware microphone timeout.
